facts.claim: Savitri chooses Satyavan herself, and the sage Narada warns that Satyavan has only one defect: he will die within a year.

sources.quote: He hath one only defect that hath overwhelmed all his virtues.

facts.claim: Told to pick another husband, Savitri refuses, saying a daughter can be given away only once and she will not choose twice.
Savitri counts the days to her husband's death and keeps the prediction constantly in mind.

sources.quote: she had counted the days as they passed

facts.claim: Satyavan goes into the forest to gather fruit and cut wood, and while working he is overcome by pain in his head.

sources.quote: O Savitri, owing to this hard exercise my head acheth, and all my limbs and my heart also are afflicted sorely!

facts.claim: Yama, the god of death, arrives in person, dark-skinned, red-eyed, robed in red, carrying a noose.

sources.quote: she saw a person clad in red attire with his head decked with a diadem

facts.claim: Yama explains he came himself rather than sending emissaries because Satyavan is too virtuous to be taken by messengers.

sources.quote: He deserveth not to be borne away by my emissaries. Therefore is it that I have come personally.

facts.claim: Yama draws Satyavan's life out of his body, binds it, and heads south while Savitri follows him on foot.

sources.quote: Yama by main force pulled out of the body of Satyavan, a person of the measure of the thumb, bound in noose

facts.claim: Savitri does not fight Yama; she follows him and argues, and he is pleased by her reasoned speech and offers her a boon.

sources.quote: I have been pleased with these words of thine couched in proper letters and accents, and based on reason. Do thou ask for a boon!

facts.claim: Each boon Yama grants excludes Satyavan's life, and Savitri's first three requests are for her father-in-law's sight, his kingdom, and sons for her father.

sources.quote: Except the life of thy husband, O thou of faultless features, I will bestow on thee any boon that thou mayst solicit!

facts.claim: Savitri's fourth boon is a hundred sons born to herself and Satyavan, which Yama grants without seeing the trap.

sources.quote: let there be a century of sons possessed of strength and prowess and capable of perpetuating our race!

facts.claim: Savitri then points out that the promised sons cannot exist without their father, and demands Satyavan's life back so Yama's own words come true.

sources.quote: the boon thou hast already given me is incapable of accomplishment without union with my husband

facts.claim: Yama concedes, unties the noose, and grants Satyavan a life of four hundred years.

sources.quote: Yama, the dispenser of justice, untied his noose

facts.claim: Satyavan wakes on Savitri's lap, believing he has slept a long time, and asks where the dark figure dragging him away has gone.

sources.quote: Alas, I have slept long! Wherefore didst thou not awake me? And where is that same sable person that was dragging me away?

facts.claim: Savitri later tells the assembled sages that Yama granted her five boons in total.

sources.quote: And he granted me five boons, of which do ye hear from me!

facts.claim: Savitri's father-in-law Dyumatsena regains his sight, and news soon arrives that his enemy is dead and his kingdom awaits him.

sources.quote: Meanwhile the mighty Dyumatsena, having regained his sight, could see everything.
